cards.title: Google DeepMind Traces 15-Year Games-AI Arc, Announces EVE Online Partnership and SIMA 2
cards.why_it_matters: DeepMind's retrospective from DQN to SIMA 2 (Gemini-powered) signals the lab's current research direction — generalist game agents — which feeds directly into real-world embodied-agent and multimodal reasoning work.
cards.summary: DeepMind reviews its games-AI lineage: DQN (2015), AlphaGo/Zero, AlphaZero, MuZero, AlphaStar, and AlphaFold (2024 Nobel). SIMA 2, powered by Gemini, is a generalist agent operating via screen pixels and keyboard/mouse — no game API needed — achieving human-like play across No Man's Sky, Valheim, and others. A new research partnership with Fenris Creations targets EVE Online gameplay.

cards.title: AI4AI-Bench: New Benchmark Tests Whether LLM Agents Can Redesign Training Algorithms (Best Score: 0.25/1.0)
cards.why_it_matters: This is a direct operational test of recursive self-improvement capability — one of the field's most consequential open questions — and the results quantify how far current frontier systems are from closing that loop.
cards.summary: AI4AI-Bench presents 10 frozen research repos spanning 10 training-algorithm families; agents get 4 hours on one B300 to rewrite the training algorithm, which is then re-run for scoring against the original. Scale: 0=uninformative model, 0.1=original algorithm, 1.0=task optimum. Across 29 configurations of 6 systems, mean score is 0.166 and the best reaches 0.250. Most submissions never change how the model learns; those that do average 0.226 vs. 0.126 for those that don't. More reasoning effort shifts the fraction that attempts algorithmic change from 8% to 64%.

cards.title: Unified Variational Framework Connects PAC-Bayes, Ville, and Azuma-Hoeffding via Martingale Path-Space
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on PAC-Bayes bounds, safe testing, or sequential hypothesis testing, this provides an exact accounting of the slack discarded by each classical inequality — useful for tightening or choosing between bounds.
cards.summary: The paper develops exact variational identities for nonneg martingales on path-time space, recovering Ville's inequality, Azuma-Hoeffding, and PAC-Bayes as special cases while characterizing what each discards. Slack has closed form in three geometries. Random stopping times incur an e-process 'peeking penalty.' Geometric mixtures of test martingales gain a pooling benefit for multi-model safe testing.

cards.title: BERT-LER: BERT-Style EHR Model Pretrained on 75M Patients Unifies Lab Value Encoding and Interpretability
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers working on clinical ML or foundation models for structured data, this is a concrete architecture combining percentile-binned lab tokens with Integrated Gradients attributions, benchmarked on the public EHRShot suite.
cards.summary: BERT-LER encodes lab results as discrete tokens via percentile-based binning within a BERT-style architecture, pretrained and fine-tuned on a de-identified EHR dataset of 75 million patients. Integrated Gradients provides token-level attributions. On EHRShot and an asthma severity task, it matches or exceeds public baselines, with stronger margins on laboratory-related sub-tasks, and attributions align with known clinical risk factors.

cards.title: Hugging Face Research: ASR Models Memorize Benchmark Transcripts, Not Audio
cards.why_it_matters: Benchmark gaming in speech recognition directly parallels evaluation inflation you should watch for in LLM and multimodal model comparisons — the methodology here is a concrete template for detecting it.
cards.summary: Testing 11 open-source ASR models, Hugging Face found several top-scorers reproduce VoxPopuli and LibriSpeech reference transcripts even when audio contradicts them or key words are silenced. Models appear to use acoustic cues to identify benchmark membership. Three new probes quantify this 'benchmaxxing,' and held-out sets in Real World VoiceEQ and Open-ASR Leaderboard aim to counter it.

cards.title: TCP_α: Margin-Controlled Confidence Target Guarantees Separation of Correct vs. Incorrect Predictions
cards.why_it_matters: Post-hoc confidence calibration with provable correct/incorrect separation is directly applicable to any production classifier where selective prediction or human-in-the-loop thresholding matters.
cards.summary: TCP_α is a post-hoc confidence estimation target that penalizes misclassified samples with a tunable margin, provably separating target values of correct and incorrect predictions regardless of class count. Evaluated on rāga identification and frame-wise ornamentation detection, rejecting the lowest-confidence 8% of predictions lifts macro-F1 from 0.89 to 0.98. Fine-tuning the confidence head with 5% labeled samples restores performance under domain shift.

cards.title: Confidence Sets for Sparse Dictionary Learning Under High Coherence With AEB Adaptive Computation
cards.why_it_matters: Relevant if you work on dictionary learning or sparse coding for scientific signals where physical interpretability of atom support matters and coherence creates ambiguity.
cards.summary: The paper addresses physical-support uncertainty in sparse pursuit over learned, highly coherent dictionaries. A cross-dictionary confidence correspondence retains calibration-compatible dictionaries and deployment-compatible sparse representations, projecting onto physical-support space. Minimax physical resolution from N calibration signals satisfies δ_opt(N,s) ∝ min{s, 1/(√N·s²)}. The proposed active endpoint bracketing (AEB) procedure evaluates only candidates that can affect the physical report, avoiding unsupported refinement with fewer evaluations.
